This reference describes that source. A deployment runs it only while the implementation behind each proxy is the one the deployment manifest records for that commit: check when you integrate and whenever a proxy emits `Upgraded` (README [Security and trust](README.md#security-and-trust)).

## Conventions

- **Addresses.** Call the proxies listed in README [Deployments](README.md#deployments). The ABIs are those of the implementations; `D20Proxy` adds no functions of its own. `D20BeaconVerifier` is not behind a proxy: its address is in each beacon registration (`beaconOf`) and in README [Deployments](README.md#deployments).
- **Units.** Fees and credits are wei of the native token of each chain, 18 decimals on both chains: USDC on Arc (`1e18` is 1 USDC), ETH on Robinhood Chain. Deadlines and timestamps are Unix seconds. Ratios are basis points (10000 is 100%).
- **Callers.** "Anyone" means any account or contract; "Any contract" means `msg.sender` must have code. Owner-only functions revert `OwnableUnauthorizedAccount` for other callers.
- **Selectors.** Functions and errors show their 4-byte selector, events their topic 0, so revert data and logs can be matched by hand.
- **Decoding errors.** `coordinatorAbi`, `epochEntropyAbi`, `beaconVerifierAbi` and `roundCoordinatorAbi` (`@d20dao/vrf-sdk/abi`) contain every custom error below. When your consumer calls the coordinator with an ordinary Solidity call, a coordinator revert is passed through unchanged, so a wallet sending a transaction to your consumer sees the coordinator's selector. Decode with `coordinator.interface.parseError(data)` in ethers or `decodeErrorResult({ abi: coordinatorAbi, data })` in viem, or build your consumer's contract object from its ABI plus the coordinator's error entries. Your consumer's own errors, such as `OnlyCoordinator` and `InvalidCoordinator` from `D20VRFConsumer`, are only in your consumer's ABI. Arithmetic overflow reverts with `Panic(uint256)`.
- **ethers v6 results.** Structs and multiple return values arrive as `Result` objects, which are arrays. A named value is also a property unless its name collides with an `Array` or `Result` member, such as `length`, `values`, `keys`, `map` or `filter`; read such a value with `result.getValue(name)`, by position, or from `result.toObject()`. Unnamed outputs, such as those of `pricing()`, are positional only.
- **Consumer contracts.** `D20VRFConsumer` implements `rawFulfillRandomness(requestId, randomness)` and `onRefund(requestId)`; both revert `OnlyCoordinator` unless called by the coordinator proxy given to its constructor, which reverts `InvalidCoordinator` for an address without code.

## <a id="coordinator"></a>D20VRFCoordinator

The consumer entry point. Call the coordinator proxy for your chain (README [Deployments](README.md#deployments)). `ID20VRF` in `contracts/interfaces/ID20VRF.sol` declares the five functions a consumer contract needs (`quoteFee`, `quoteFeeAt`, `requestRandomness`, `requestMappedRandomness`, `getMappedResult`); `coordinatorAbi` from `@d20dao/vrf-sdk/abi` carries everything below. In Solidity, declare a local interface for any other function you call.

Requests, fulfillment, `storeBlockHash`, retries, `refundRequest` and withdrawals are `nonReentrant`. A consumer callback (`rawFulfillRandomness`, `onRefund`) that calls one of them fails with `ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall`, and the coordinator records the callback as failed. Views stay callable from callbacks.

### <a id="coordinator-types"></a>Types

#### <a id="coordinator-type-d20vrfcoordinator-request"></a>`D20VRFCoordinator.Request`

Returned by `getRequest`. It does not contain the escrowed fee or the refund ratio; read `requestFeePaid` and `requestRefundBps`.

Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 61–79

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `consumer` | `address` | Contract that made the request; receives `rawFulfillRandomness` and `onRefund`. |
| `callbackGasLimit` | `uint32` | Gas forwarded to `rawFulfillRandomness` at fulfillment, and the lowest `gasLimit` that `retryCallback` accepts. |
| `requestBlock` | `uint64` | Block of the request transaction. |
| `targetBlock` | `uint64` | Block whose hash enters the seed: `max(requestBlock, committedBlock + 1)` of the epoch. 0 until the epoch packet is published. |
| `deadline` | `uint64` | Request block timestamp plus `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` (60 seconds), in Unix seconds. A proof accepted in a block with timestamp at or before `deadline` serves the request; `refundRequest` needs a block timestamp after it. |
| `refundAddress` | `address` | Fixed recipient of the expiry refund and of any overpayment credit. |
| `clientSeed` | `bytes32` | Value supplied by the consumer, bound into the seed and emitted in `RandomnessRequested`. |
| `mappingHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256(abi.encode(operation, lower, upper, count, population))` of the stored spec; `hashMapping(spec)` in TypeScript. |
| `blockHash` | `bytes32` | Target block hash once `storeBlockHash` or fulfillment stored it; zero before. |
| `randomness` | `bytes32` | Accepted VRF output. Zero until `fulfilled`. |
| `proofHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256(abi.encode(proof))` of the accepted proof. Zero until `fulfilled`. |
| `transcriptHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256(abi.encode(TRANSCRIPT_DOMAIN, chainId, coordinator, requestId, protocolConfigurationHash, blockHash, proofHash, randomness, mappingHash, epochId, epochHash))`. Zero until `fulfilled`. |
| `fulfilled` | `bool` | A proof was accepted. Final: the word can no longer change. |
| `delivered` | `bool` | A callback attempt succeeded. Stays false after a failed callback until `retryCallback` succeeds; it says nothing about acceptance. |
| `refunded` | `bool` | `refundRequest` settled the request. Never true together with `fulfilled`. |
| `epochId` | `uint64` | Epoch of `requestBlock`, fixed at creation; never zero for an existing request. |
| `epochHash` | `bytes32` | Commitment of the published epoch packet. Zero until the packet is published. |

#### <a id="coordinator-type-randomnessmapping-spec"></a>`RandomnessMapping.Spec`

A randomness mapping stored with a request ("mapping" here is not a Solidity `mapping`). The TypeScript `MappingSpec` returned by `builtins` has the same five fields in the same order, with `lower` and `upper` as `bigint`, and ethers encodes it for this struct unchanged. Valid combinations: README [Randomness options](README.md#randomness-options).

Source: `libraries/RandomnessMapping.sol` lines 7–14

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `operation` | `RandomnessMapping.Operation` | Enum encoded as uint8: 0 Raw, 1 DiceRoll, 2 CoinFlip, 3 NumberRange, 4 ChooseOne, 5 ChooseMany, 6 Shuffle. |
| `lower` | `uint256` | NumberRange minimum; zero for every other operation. |
| `upper` | `uint256` | DiceRoll sides or NumberRange maximum; zero otherwise. |
| `count` | `uint32` | Values returned: the dice count; 1 for CoinFlip, NumberRange and ChooseOne; the number of choices for ChooseMany; the population for Shuffle; 0 for Raw. |
| `population` | `uint32` | Number of items (1 to 256) for ChooseOne, ChooseMany and Shuffle; zero otherwise. |

#### <a id="coordinator-type-vrf-proof"></a>`VRF.Proof`

Chainlink secp256k1 VRF proof, verified by the unmodified vendored `VRF.sol`. ABI-encoded it is 416 bytes: the `FulfillmentEvidence` packet.

Source: `vendor/VRF.sol` lines 570–580

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pk` | `uint256[2]` | VRF public key; must equal `(publicKeyX, publicKeyY)`. |
| `gamma` | `uint256[2]` | Proof point. The accepted word is `keccak256(abi.encode(3, gamma))`. |
| `c` | `uint256` | Proof challenge scalar. |
| `s` | `uint256` | Proof response scalar. |
| `seed` | `uint256` | Must equal `requestSeed(requestId)`. |
| `uWitness` | `address` | Address of `c·pk + s·G`, checked by the verifier. |
| `cGammaWitness` | `uint256[2]` | Precomputed `c·gamma`, checked by the verifier. |
| `sHashWitness` | `uint256[2]` | Precomputed `s·hashToCurve(pk, seed)`, checked by the verifier. |
| `zInv` | `uint256` | Inverse of the projective z coordinate of `cGammaWitness + sHashWitness`. |

### <a id="coordinator-requesting"></a>Requesting

Requests must come from a contract and pay at least the fee computed in their own transaction; see README [Paying for a request](README.md#paying-for-a-request). The registry call a request makes (`checkpointEpoch` for the current epoch) cannot fail in practice, so requests revert only with the errors listed.

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-quotefee"></a>`quoteFee`

```solidity
function quoteFee(uint32 callbackGasLimit) external view returns (uint256)
```

Selector `0xc9caa0c3` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 232–237

Fee for a request with this `callbackGasLimit` priced at `block.basefee`, that is `quoteFeeAt(callbackGasLimit, block.basefee)`. Exact inside the requesting transaction, which is how `D20VRFRequests` helpers pay. Through `eth_call` the base fee is commonly reported as 0 (observed on Arc), so the answer collapses to `minFee` and a transaction sent with it reverts `IncorrectFee`. Off-chain, quote with `quoteFeeAt` and the latest header base fee plus a buffer, as `quoteRequestFee` does. It does not check the gas limit range.

**Errors:** [`FeeOverflow`](#coordinator-error-feeoverflow).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-quotefeeat"></a>`quoteFeeAt`

```solidity
function quoteFeeAt(uint32 callbackGasLimit, uint256 baseFee) external view returns (uint256)
```

Selector `0x26fa8481` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 224–231

`max(minFee, feeMultiplier × baseFee × (fulfillGasOverhead + callbackGasLimit))` over the live pricing for a base fee in wei that you supply; with `feeMultiplier` 0 it returns `minFee`. A quote, not a reservation: pricing can change before your transaction. A `baseFee` large enough to overflow uint256 reverts with `Panic(0x11)` instead of `FeeOverflow`.

**Errors:** [`FeeOverflow`](#coordinator-error-feeoverflow).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-requestrandomness"></a>`requestRandomness`

```solidity
function requestRandomness(bytes32 clientSeed, uint32 callbackGasLimit, address _refundAddress) external payable returns (uint256 requestId)
```

Selector `0x9849d1e5` · Caller: Any contract · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 239–244, 252–291

Creates a raw request (spec all zero) with `msg.sender` as consumer and returns its ID. Needs `msg.value` at least the fee computed in this transaction; escrows exactly that fee and credits any excess to `_refundAddress` as refund credit. Fixes the request block, epoch, client seed, refund address, fee, refund ratio (`refundBps`) and a deadline of `block.timestamp + RESPONSE_TIMEOUT`. After acceptance the consumer receives `rawFulfillRandomness(requestId, randomness)` with exactly `callbackGasLimit` gas. Checks run in this order: caller has code, refund address non-zero, gas limit in range, fee, mapping, epoch started.

**Emits:** [`FeeOverpaymentCredited`](#coordinator-event-feeoverpaymentcredited), [`RandomnessRequested`](#coordinator-event-randomnessrequested), [`MappingRequested`](#coordinator-event-mappingrequested).

**Errors:** [`ContractConsumerRequired`](#coordinator-error-contractconsumerrequired), [`InvalidRefundAddress`](#coordinator-error-invalidrefundaddress), [`InvalidCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-invalidcallbackgas), [`FeeOverflow`](#coordinator-error-feeoverflow), [`IncorrectFee`](#coordinator-error-incorrectfee), [`EpochUnavailable`](#coordinator-error-epochunavailable).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-requestmappedrandomness"></a>`requestMappedRandomness`

```solidity
function requestMappedRandomness(bytes32 clientSeed, uint32 callbackGasLimit, address _refundAddress, RandomnessMapping.Spec spec) external payable returns (uint256 requestId)
```

Selector `0xe6b41a8c` · Caller: Any contract · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 246–250, 252–291

Same as `requestRandomness`, storing `spec` with the request (`getMapping`, `mappingHash`). The callback still carries the raw word; read the mapped values with `getMappedResult`. `D20VRFRequests` helpers call this function and pay `quoteFee` from the calling contract balance.

**Emits:** [`FeeOverpaymentCredited`](#coordinator-event-feeoverpaymentcredited), [`RandomnessRequested`](#coordinator-event-randomnessrequested), [`MappingRequested`](#coordinator-event-mappingrequested).

**Errors:** [`ContractConsumerRequired`](#coordinator-error-contractconsumerrequired), [`InvalidRefundAddress`](#coordinator-error-invalidrefundaddress), [`InvalidCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-invalidcallbackgas), [`FeeOverflow`](#coordinator-error-feeoverflow), [`IncorrectFee`](#coordinator-error-incorrectfee), [`InvalidMapping`](#coordinator-error-invalidmapping), [`EpochUnavailable`](#coordinator-error-epochunavailable).

Views, callable by anyone. They describe requests created from now on; an existing request settles from its own snapshots (`requestFeePaid`, `requestRefundBps`).

| <a id="coordinator-fn-minfee"></a>`minFee() returns (uint256)` | `0x24ec7590` | Minimum fee in wei, at most `MAX_MIN_FEE` (10 USDC). | line 46 |

### <a id="coordinator-reading-request-state-and-results"></a>Reading request state and results

Views, callable by anyone, including from a callback. Request IDs start at 1 and increase by one; functions taking a `requestId` revert `UnknownRequest` for an ID that was never issued. README [Reading results](README.md#reading-results) shows a polling loop.

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-getrequest"></a>`getRequest`

```solidity
function getRequest(uint256 requestId) external view returns (D20VRFCoordinator.Request result)
```

Selector `0xc58343ef` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 293–312, 575–580

Full state of a request, see [`D20VRFCoordinator.Request`](#coordinator-type-d20vrfcoordinator-request). `targetBlock` and `epochHash` are resolved from the registry, so they become non-zero as soon as the epoch packet is published. `fulfilled` means the word is final; `delivered` only reports that a callback succeeded. A request that is not `fulfilled` in a block whose timestamp is after `deadline` has expired and can only be refunded. When polling, read the latest block before `getRequest`, so that a proof included up to that block is visible.

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-getmapping"></a>`getMapping`

```solidity
function getMapping(uint256 requestId) external view returns (RandomnessMapping.Spec)
```

Selector `0xede9ba8b` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 344–347

The stored [`RandomnessMapping.Spec`](#coordinator-type-randomnessmapping-spec); all fields zero (Raw) for `requestRandomness`.

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-getmappedresult"></a>`getMappedResult`

```solidity
function getMappedResult(uint256 requestId) external view returns (uint256[])
```

Selector `0x8f09a3e6` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 349–353

The accepted word mapped with the stored spec: `[uint256(word)]` for a raw request, otherwise the values in README [Randomness options](README.md#randomness-options). Part of `ID20VRF`. Reverts `NotFulfilled` until a proof is accepted, so an expired or refunded request never has a result. Gas grows with the mapping; a 256-item shuffle is expensive onchain.

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`NotFulfilled`](#coordinator-error-notfulfilled).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-maprandomness"></a>`mapRandomness`

```solidity
function mapRandomness(bytes32 randomness, RandomnessMapping.Spec spec) external pure returns (uint256[])
```

Selector `0x41c2a199` · Caller: Anyone (pure) · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 355–360

Maps any word with any valid spec, like the SDK `mapRandomness(word, spec)` off-chain. It does not show that a request was fulfilled.

**Errors:** [`InvalidMapping`](#coordinator-error-invalidmapping).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-requestfeepaid"></a>`requestFeePaid`

```solidity
function requestFeePaid(uint256 requestId) external view returns (uint256)
```

Selector `0xef7cc992` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 335–338

Fee escrowed by the request (`feePaid` in `RandomnessRequested`), excluding any overpayment. The keeper share, the protocol share and the refund are computed from it.

### <a id="coordinator-settlement-refunds-and-credits"></a>Settlement, refunds and credits

Recovery calls need no value or role. They forward gas to the consumer and revert `InsufficientCallbackGas` rather than forward less, so the transaction gas limit must cover it (README [Gas for refund and retry calls](README.md#gas-for-refund-and-retry-calls)). Refund credit and keeper credit are pull balances: only the holder withdraws them.

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-refundrequest"></a>`refundRequest`

```solidity
function refundRequest(uint256 requestId) external
```

Selector `0x7411484e` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 483–507, 519–530

Refunds an unfulfilled request once a block timestamp is after its deadline. Marks it refunded, sends `feePaid × requestRefundBps / 10000` to the fixed refund address with a 30,000-gas transfer, or adds it to that address's refund credit if the transfer fails, and adds the rest of the fee to `earnedFees`. Then calls `onRefund(requestId)` on the consumer with 100,000 gas; a failed notification does not undo the refund. The caller receives nothing. Measured minimum transaction gas limit 302,558 to 357,517; use 400,000.

**Emits:** [`RequestRefundedTo`](#coordinator-event-requestrefundedto), [`RefundCallbackAttempted`](#coordinator-event-refundcallbackattempted).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`RefundNotAvailable`](#coordinator-error-refundnotavailable), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-insufficientcallbackgas).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-retrycallback"></a>`retryCallback`

```solidity
function retryCallback(uint256 requestId, uint32 gasLimit) external
```

Selector `0xdd11c275` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 473–481, 630–647

Calls `rawFulfillRandomness` again with the same accepted word after a failed callback, forwarding `gasLimit` (30,000 to 1,000,000 and not below the request's `callbackGasLimit`). Sets `delivered` on success. Pays nobody and never changes the word. Transaction gas limit: about `gasLimit + 250,000`.

**Emits:** [`CallbackAttempted`](#coordinator-event-callbackattempted).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`NotFulfilled`](#coordinator-error-notfulfilled), [`AlreadyDelivered`](#coordinator-error-alreadydelivered), [`InvalidCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-invalidcallbackgas), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-insufficientcallbackgas).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-retryrefundcallback"></a>`retryRefundCallback`

```solidity
function retryRefundCallback(uint256 requestId, uint32 gasLimit) external
```

Selector `0x054f6962` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 509–517, 519–530

Repeats a failed `onRefund` notification for a refunded request with `gasLimit` (100,000 to 1,000,000). Never transfers funds again. Transaction gas limit: about `gasLimit + 150,000`.

**Emits:** [`RefundCallbackAttempted`](#coordinator-event-refundcallbackattempted).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`NotRefunded`](#coordinator-error-notrefunded), [`RefundCallbackAlreadyDelivered`](#coordinator-error-refundcallbackalreadydelivered), [`InvalidCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-invalidcallbackgas), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-insufficientcallbackgas).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-withdrawrefundcredit"></a>`withdrawRefundCredit`

```solidity
function withdrawRefundCredit(address recipient) external
```

Selector `0x445071f2` · Caller: Refund-credit holder · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 532–542

Sends all of the caller's refund credit, `refundCredits(msg.sender)`, to `recipient` with all remaining gas. Credit comes from overpayment and from refund transfers that failed, and belongs to the request's refund address, so that address must make the call. If `recipient` rejects the transfer the call reverts and the credit stays.

**Emits:** [`RefundCreditWithdrawn`](#coordinator-event-refundcreditwithdrawn).

**Errors:** [`InvalidRefundAddress`](#coordinator-error-invalidrefundaddress), [`NoRefundCredit`](#coordinator-error-norefundcredit), [`TransferFailed`](#coordinator-error-transferfailed).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-withdrawfees"></a>`withdrawFees`

```solidity
function withdrawFees(address recipient) external
```

Selector `0x164e68de` · Caller: Fee recipient · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 544–553

### <a id="coordinator-keeper-and-proof-functions"></a>Keeper and proof functions

Proof submission is permissionless: anyone holding a valid proof may submit it, and the keeper share goes to the submitting wallet when the registry authorizes it as its committer or a backup committer, and to `committer()` otherwise. Consumers normally only read `getRequest`. Besides the custom errors listed, proof functions can revert with `Error(string)` messages from the vendored VRF verifier, such as `invalid proof`, which are not in the ABI.

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-fulfillrandomness"></a>`fulfillRandomness`

```solidity
function fulfillRandomness(uint256 requestId, VRF.Proof proof) external
```

Selector `0xef7c2b19` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 393–401, 430–465

Accepts a proof for a request that is not fulfilled, not refunded and not past its deadline; acceptance in a block with timestamp equal to `deadline` is timely. Stores the target block hash if needed, verifies the proof against `requestSeed(requestId)`, stores the word, proof hash and transcript hash, sets `fulfilled`, adds `feePaid` minus the keeper share to `earnedFees` and calls the consumer with `callbackGasLimit` gas. It then sends the keeper share (`keeperFeeBps` of `feePaid`) with 30,000 gas to the submitting wallet when the registry answers `isAuthorizedCommitter` true for it (the committer or an allowed backup committer) and to `committer()` otherwise, or records it as that wallet's keeper credit; a registry call that reverts also pays `committer()`. A failing callback does not revert the fulfillment.

**Emits:** [`BlockHashStored`](#coordinator-event-blockhashstored), [`RequestServed`](#coordinator-event-requestserved), [`ProofVerified`](#coordinator-event-proofverified), [`RandomnessFulfilled`](#coordinator-event-randomnessfulfilled), [`FulfillmentEvidence`](#coordinator-event-fulfillmentevidence), [`CallbackAttempted`](#coordinator-event-callbackattempted), [`KeeperFeePaid`](#coordinator-event-keeperfeepaid).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`AlreadyFulfilled`](#coordinator-error-alreadyfulfilled), [`RequestRefunded`](#coordinator-error-requestrefunded), [`RequestExpired`](#coordinator-error-requestexpired), [`NotReady`](#coordinator-error-notready), [`BlockHashUnavailable`](#coordinator-error-blockhashunavailable), [`WrongPublicKey`](#coordinator-error-wrongpublickey), [`WrongSeed`](#coordinator-error-wrongseed), [`EvidencePacketTooLarge`](#coordinator-error-evidencepackettoolarge), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-insufficientcallbackgas).

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-fulfillrandomnessbatch"></a>`fulfillRandomnessBatch`

```solidity
function fulfillRandomnessBatch(uint256[] ids, VRF.Proof[] proofs) external
```

Selector `0x9497b180` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 403–428

Fulfills up to `MAX_FULFILL_BATCH` (16) requests, one proof each. Members already fulfilled, refunded or past their deadline, including an ID repeated in the batch, are skipped with `FulfillmentSkipped`; every other member runs exactly like `fulfillRandomness` and emits the same events, so an unknown ID, an unready member or an invalid proof reverts the whole batch. Before any result is revealed it checks that the gas left covers every member that will be served, `140,000 + Σ(callbackGasLimit + callbackGasLimit / 63 + 400,000)`, and reverts `InsufficientCallbackGas` otherwise, so no callback can starve a later member and revert results already revealed.

**Emits:** [`FulfillmentSkipped`](#coordinator-event-fulfillmentskipped), [`BlockHashStored`](#coordinator-event-blockhashstored), [`RequestServed`](#coordinator-event-requestserved), [`ProofVerified`](#coordinator-event-proofverified), [`RandomnessFulfilled`](#coordinator-event-randomnessfulfilled), [`FulfillmentEvidence`](#coordinator-event-fulfillmentevidence), [`CallbackAttempted`](#coordinator-event-callbackattempted), [`KeeperFeePaid`](#coordinator-event-keeperfeepaid).

**Errors:** [`InvalidBatch`](#coordinator-error-invalidbatch), [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`NotReady`](#coordinator-error-notready), [`BlockHashUnavailable`](#coordinator-error-blockhashunavailable), [`WrongPublicKey`](#coordinator-error-wrongpublickey), [`WrongSeed`](#coordinator-error-wrongseed), [`EvidencePacketTooLarge`](#coordinator-error-evidencepackettoolarge), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#coordinator-error-insufficientcallbackgas).

```solidity
function storeBlockHash(uint256 requestId) external returns (bytes32)
```

Selector `0x262fd733` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 372–376, 581–596

Resolves the target block from the published epoch, stores its hash if not stored yet and returns it. Fulfillment does this automatically; calling it earlier keeps a request provable after its target leaves the 256-block `BLOCKHASH` window. Needs `block.number` at least `targetBlock + confirmationBlocks`. Works on any request, whatever its status.

**Emits:** [`BlockHashStored`](#coordinator-event-blockhashstored).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`NotReady`](#coordinator-error-notready), [`BlockHashUnavailable`](#coordinator-error-blockhashunavailable).


Returns the word a proof yields for the request's seed, without changing state. A valid proof is not acceptance: check `getRequest(requestId).fulfilled`.

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`NotReady`](#coordinator-error-notready), [`BlockHashUnavailable`](#coordinator-error-blockhashunavailable), [`WrongPublicKey`](#coordinator-error-wrongpublickey), [`WrongSeed`](#coordinator-error-wrongseed).

Available only after publication and `confirmationBlocks` confirmations of the target block.

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#coordinator-error-unknownrequest), [`NotReady`](#coordinator-error-notready), [`BlockHashUnavailable`](#coordinator-error-blockhashunavailable).

`requestSeed` together with `deadline`, `fulfilled` and `refunded`. It reverts `NotReady` like `requestSeed`, so it is not a status read for waiting requests; use `getRequest`.


Scans `limit` (1 to 256) request IDs from `fromId` (at least 1) and returns those not fulfilled, not refunded and not past their deadline, with the ID to continue from. Continue with `nextCursor` until it equals `nextRequestId()`. The answer can be stale by the time a transaction lands.

### <a id="coordinator-owner-administration"></a>Owner administration

Owner-only functions revert `OwnableUnauthorizedAccount` for anyone else. No setter can change an existing request, the VRF key, the registry or the confirmations.

#### <a id="coordinator-fn-setpricing"></a>`setPricing`


Selector `0x4c729ce6` · Caller: Owner · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 207–214

Affects requests created afterwards; open requests keep their escrowed fee.

### <a id="coordinator-errors"></a>Errors

**Requesting**

#### <a id="coordinator-error-contractconsumerrequired"></a>`ContractConsumerRequired`

`error ContractConsumerRequired()` · Selector `0x2b99db1e` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 113, 255

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestmappedrandomness).

The caller of a request function has no code: an externally owned account, or a contract still running its constructor.

**What to do:** Send the request through a deployed consumer contract (README [Integrate a consumer](README.md#integrate-a-consumer)), and not from its constructor.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-invalidrefundaddress"></a>`InvalidRefundAddress`

`error InvalidRefundAddress()` · Selector `0xe2fe2726` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 127, 256, 534

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestmappedrandomness), [`withdrawRefundCredit`](#coordinator-fn-withdrawrefundcredit).

A request named the zero address as refund address, or `withdrawRefundCredit` named the zero address as recipient.

**What to do:** Pass a non-zero address that can receive a plain native transfer or call `withdrawRefundCredit`.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-invalidcallbackgas"></a>`InvalidCallbackGas`

`error InvalidCallbackGas()` · Selector `0x35883c54` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 115, 479, 515, 626–628

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestmappedrandomness), [`retryCallback`](#coordinator-fn-retrycallback), [`retryRefundCallback`](#coordinator-fn-retryrefundcallback).

A gas limit is out of range: a request `callbackGasLimit` outside 30,000 to 1,000,000; a `retryCallback` limit outside that range or below the request's `callbackGasLimit`; a `retryRefundCallback` limit outside 100,000 to 1,000,000.

**What to do:** Use a limit inside the range; retry with at least the original limit.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-incorrectfee"></a>`IncorrectFee`

`error IncorrectFee(uint256 expected, uint256 actual)` · Selector `0xdcf6afcb` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 114, 259

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestmappedrandomness).

`actual` (`msg.value`) is below `expected`, the fee computed in the request transaction. No request was created.

**What to do:** Quote again with `quoteFeeAt(callbackGasLimit, latestBlock.baseFeePerGas)` plus a buffer (`quoteRequestFee`) and resend. A contract paying in the same transaction sends `quoteFee(callbackGasLimit)`. Never quote with `quoteFee` through `eth_call`.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-feeoverflow"></a>`FeeOverflow`

`error FeeOverflow()` · Selector `0x8181adca` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 138, 229

**Raised by:** [`quoteFee`](#coordinator-fn-quotefee), [`quoteFeeAt`](#coordinator-fn-quotefeeat), [`requestRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestmappedrandomness).

The dynamic fee exceeds the uint96 escrow limit. Within the pricing bounds that needs a base fee above about 1.3e21 wei.

**What to do:** Not expected on a live chain. For `quoteFeeAt`, check that `baseFee` is in wei.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-invalidmapping"></a>`InvalidMapping`

`error InvalidMapping()` · Selector `0x07a966e0` · Source: `libraries/RandomnessMapping.sol` lines 19, 21–39

**Raised by:** [`requestMappedRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestmappedrandomness), [`mapRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-maprandomness).

The spec breaks the rules for its operation (README [Randomness options](README.md#randomness-options)). Declared in `RandomnessMapping`.

**What to do:** Build specs with the `D20VRFRequests` helpers or TypeScript `builtins`, which enforce the same bounds.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-epochunavailable"></a>`EpochUnavailable`

`error EpochUnavailable()` · Selector `0x0b3487b8` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 111, 263

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-requestmappedrandomness).

The request block is before the registry's first epoch: `epochForBlock(block.number)` is 0.

**What to do:** Not expected on the Arc deployments, whose epochs have started. Check that you call the coordinator proxy for your chain; on a new deployment, wait for `firstEpochStart`.

**Reading and recovery**

#### <a id="coordinator-error-unknownrequest"></a>`UnknownRequest`

`error UnknownRequest()` · Selector `0x6d080297` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 116, 566–569

**Raised by:** [`getRequest`](#coordinator-fn-getrequest), [`getMapping`](#coordinator-fn-getmapping), [`getMappedResult`](#coordinator-fn-getmappedresult), [`requestFeePaid`](#coordinator-fn-requestfeepaid), [`requestRefundBps`](#coordinator-fn-requestrefundbps), [`refundRequest`](#coordinator-fn-refundrequest), [`retryCallback`](#coordinator-fn-retrycallback), [`retryRefundCallback`](#coordinator-fn-retryrefundcallback), [`fulfillRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-fulfillrandomness), [`fulfillRandomnessBatch`](#coordinator-fn-fulfillrandomnessbatch), [`storeBlockHash`](#coordinator-fn-storeblockhash), [`verifyRequestProof`](#coordinator-fn-verifyrequestproof), [`requestSeed`](#coordinator-fn-requestseed), [`getProofContext`](#coordinator-fn-getproofcontext).

No request has this ID: 0, or not below `nextRequestId()`. An unknown ID also reverts a whole `fulfillRandomnessBatch`.

**What to do:** Take `requestId` from the `RandomnessRequested` log of the request receipt, and read from the same chain and coordinator proxy.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-notfulfilled"></a>`NotFulfilled`

`error NotFulfilled()` · Selector `0x07bc6c3e` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 120, 351, 476

**What to do:** Poll `getRequest(requestId)` until `fulfilled`. Once a block timestamp is after `deadline` without fulfillment, the request has expired and only `refundRequest` applies.

**Raised by:** [`refundRequest`](#coordinator-fn-refundrequest).

`refundRequest` on a request that is fulfilled, already refunded, or not yet past its deadline (the block timestamp must be greater than `deadline`).

**What to do:** Read `getRequest`: use the result if `fulfilled`, stop if `refunded`, otherwise retry after a block with a later timestamp than `deadline`.

`retryRefundCallback` on a request that has not been refunded.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-refundcallbackalreadydelivered"></a>`RefundCallbackAlreadyDelivered`

`error RefundCallbackAlreadyDelivered()` · Selector `0x6502f8ae` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 134, 513

**Raised by:** [`retryRefundCallback`](#coordinator-fn-retryrefundcallback).

`retryRefundCallback` after an `onRefund` notification already succeeded (`refundCallbackDelivered`).

**What to do:** Nothing to retry.

#### <a id="coordinator-error-insufficientcallbackgas"></a>`InsufficientCallbackGas`

`error InsufficientCallbackGas()` · Selector `0xa2c23f0d` · Source: `D20VRFCoordinator.sol` lines 124, 421, 497, 522, 638–639

**Raised by:** [`refundRequest`](#coordinator-fn-refundrequest), [`retryCallback`](#coordinator-fn-retrycallback), [`retryRefundCallback`](#coordinator-fn-retryrefundcallback), [`fulfillRandomness`](#coordinator-fn-fulfillrandomness), [`fulfillRandomnessBatch`](#coordinator-fn-fulfillrandomnessbatch).

Too little gas remained to forward the full callback budget and keep the coordinator's reserve: `gasLimit + gasLimit/63 + 140,000` before a fulfillment callback, `100,000 + 100,000/63 + 140,000` after refund settlement, `gasLimit + gasLimit/63 + 50,000` before a refund notification, and `140,000 + Σ(callbackGasLimit + callbackGasLimit / 63 + 400,000)` over the served members before `fulfillRandomnessBatch` reveals any result. The coordinator reverts instead of forwarding less.

**What to do:** Raise the transaction gas limit: 400,000 for `refundRequest`, `gasLimit + 250,000` for `retryCallback`, `gasLimit + 150,000` for `retryRefundCallback` (README [Gas for refund and retry calls](README.md#gas-for-refund-and-retry-calls)); a keeper sizes a batch to the sum above. `eth_estimateGas` finds the minimum.

## <a id="registry"></a>EpochEntropy

The epoch registry. A consumer never needs to call it: a request fixes its epoch automatically, and the coordinator reads the registry for targets and for the keeper-share recipient. The first group and the events matter to consumers and verifiers (README [Replay and verification](README.md#replay-and-verification)); publication and administration are listed for completeness.

Epoch sources are recipes in an owner-managed, append-only registry: each has an id, a canonical request whose `keccak256` is the query hash its signer signs, a data template that fixes the exact signed bytes the registry accepts (README [Data templates](README.md#data-templates)) and the body keepers send: the JSON they post to the provider gateway, or a beacon's canonical request. A catalog lists 1 to `MAX_SOURCES` registered recipes with one signer each; each epoch selects from the catalog in force for it (`catalogAt`).

A recipe is one of two kinds. A signed API recipe (`registerRecipe`) commits a provider's signed record: the signature is an EIP-191 signature of the recipe's signer over the query hash, timestamp and data. A beacon recipe (`registerBeacon`) commits one round of a public randomness beacon such as drand: the data is the round number, the timestamp the round's scheduled time and the signature the beacon's, which the verifier recorded in its registration (`beaconOf`) checks. Its catalog signer is `slotSigner(recipe)`, an identity derived from the registration. Replay needs the registration of every beacon recipe an epoch used (README [Beacon epochs](README.md#beacon-epochs)).

### <a id="registry-types"></a>Types

#### <a id="registry-type-epochentropy-epoch"></a>`EpochEntropy.Epoch`

Returned by `getEpoch`; all zero until the epoch is published.

Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 57–60

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `epochHash` | `bytes32` | Epoch commitment: `keccak256(abi.encode(EPOCH_DOMAIN, chainId, registry, catalogHash, epochId, epochStart, anchorHash, source, queryHash, dataHash, attestationHash))`. |
| `catalogHash` | `bytes32` | Hash of the catalog in force for the epoch (`catalogAt`) at publication. |
| `anchorHash` | `bytes32` | Hash of block `epochStart - 1`, which selects the source. |
| `source` | `uint8` | Committed slot in the epoch's catalog, 0 to `sourceCountAt(epochId) - 1`: the selected slot or a fallback. The recipe is the catalog's recipe at that slot. |
| `queryHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256` of the canonical request of the slot's recipe. |
| `dataHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256` of the signed response data. |
| `attestationHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256(abi.encode(queryHash, timestamp, dataHash, keccak256(signature)))`. |
| `signedAt` | `uint256` | Attestation timestamp in Unix seconds. |
| `committedBlock` | `uint64` | Publication block. Requests of the epoch target `max(requestBlock, committedBlock + 1)`. |

#### <a id="registry-type-epochentropy-selection"></a>`EpochEntropy.Selection`

Returned by `getEpochSelection` and `getEpochFallbackSelection`.

Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 55–56, 345–356

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `uint8` | Slot in the epoch's catalog. |
| `recipe` | `uint8` | Registered recipe id at that slot. |
| `airnode` | `address` | Signer of that slot in the catalog in force for the epoch; for a beacon recipe its `slotSigner`. |
| `selector` | `bytes32` | `keccak256(abi.encode(SELECT_DOMAIN, catalogHash, epochId, anchor))`; the slot is `(selector mod count + attempt) mod count` with `count = sourceCountAt(epochId)`. |
| `queryHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256` of `canonicalRequest`. |
| `canonicalRequest` | `string` | Canonical request of the recipe, as `getRecipe` returns it. |

#### <a id="registry-type-epochentropy-attestation"></a>`EpochEntropy.Attestation`

Source response passed to `commitEpoch` and `commitEpochFallback`: a signed API record or a beacon round.

Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 54, 363–391

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `timestamp` | `uint256` | Signing time in Unix seconds, or for a beacon round its scheduled time `genesis + (round - 1) × period`; not in the future and at most `MAX_ATTESTATION_AGE` old at publication. |
| `data` | `bytes` | Signed response bytes, or for a beacon the round number in decimal, at most `MAX_DATA_BYTES` (128), matching the data template of the slot's recipe exactly. |
| `signature` | `bytes` | For a signed API recipe, the 65-byte signature over `toEthSignedMessageHash(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(queryHash, timestamp, data)))`. For a beacon recipe, the beacon's 64-byte signature of the round, which the registered verifier checks. |

#### <a id="registry-type-epochentropy-beacon"></a>`EpochEntropy.Beacon`

Returned by `beaconOf`: the registration of a beacon recipe. Fixed when `registerBeacon` appends the recipe. All zero for a signed API recipe.

Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 64–66

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verifier` | `address` | Contract that checks a round's signature under `publicKey` (`IBeaconVerifier`, for drand's evmnet `D20BeaconVerifier`). Zero marks a signed API recipe. |
| `genesis` | `uint64` | Scheduled time of round 1, Unix seconds. Round `r` is scheduled at `genesis + (r - 1) × period`. |
| `period` | `uint64` | Seconds between rounds. |
| `chainHash` | `bytes32` | Identifier of the beacon network (for drand, the chain hash), 32 bytes. The recipe's canonical request is `["drand","<chainHash>"]`. |
| `publicKey` | `bytes` | The beacon's group public key as the verifier reads it; for `D20BeaconVerifier` 128 bytes, `x_im ‖ x_re ‖ y_im ‖ y_re` of a BN254 G2 point. |

A registered recipe: `queryHash` (`keccak256` of `canonicalRequest`), the canonical request its signer signs, the data template its signed data must match and the body keepers send: the JSON they post to the provider gateway, or for a beacon recipe its canonical request. #### <a id="registry-fn-slotsigner"></a>`slotSigner`

```solidity

```

Selector `0xb42be3c1` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 193–199

The signer a catalog lists for a beacon recipe: the low 160 bits of `keccak256(abi.encode(BEACON_DOMAIN, verifier, chainHash, keccak256(publicKey), genesis, period))`, an identity derived from the registration and not a key. Zero for a signed API recipe and for an id that is not registered. `scheduleCatalog` requires it as the signer of a beacon slot; `beaconSlotSigner` in `@d20dao/vrf-sdk` computes it off-chain.

#### <a id="registry-fn-verifybeacon"></a>`verifyBeacon`

```solidity
function verifyBeacon(uint8 recipe, uint64 round, bytes signature) external view returns (bool)
```

Selector `0x0ccd9ab2` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 200–209

Whether `signature` is the valid signature of `round` for a beacon recipe, checked the way a publication checks it: the recipe's verifier is called with a fixed allowance of `BEACON_VERIFY_GAS` and only an exact `true` counts. False for a signed API recipe and for an id that is not registered. For a beacon recipe it reverts `BeaconGasTooLow`, and never answers false, when the gas of the call cannot give the verifier its whole allowance; an `eth_call` needs about 461,000 gas.

**Errors:** [`BeaconGasTooLow`](#registry-error-beacongastoolow).

#### <a id="registry-fn-commitepoch"></a>`commitEpoch`

```solidity
function commitEpoch(uint64 epochId, EpochEntropy.Attestation a) external
```

Selector `0xb1580277` · Caller: Committer or backup committer · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 357, 363–391

Publishes the packet of the selected source once per epoch, from the epoch start: checks that the attestation is not future-dated and at most 240 seconds old and that its data matches the data template of the slot's recipe exactly, then checks its signature. For a signed API recipe the slot's signer in the epoch's catalog must have signed it. For a beacon recipe the timestamp must be the scheduled time of the round in the data, and the verifier of its registration must accept the signature of that round within `BEACON_VERIFY_GAS`; the call reverts `BeaconGasTooLow` when the gas left cannot give the verifier that allowance. Stores the record and emits the packet. Publishing earns nothing by itself: the keeper share of each request goes to the authorized wallet that submits its accepted proof, or to `committer()` when the submitter is not authorized.

**Emits:** [`EpochCommitted`](#registry-event-epochcommitted).

### <a id="registry-recipes-and-catalogs"></a>Recipes and catalogs

Owner-only; on Arc Mainnet the owner is the DAO treasury Safe. A recipe or catalog never changes a published epoch.

#### <a id="registry-fn-registerrecipe"></a>`registerRecipe`

```solidity
function registerRecipe(string canonicalRequest, bytes template, string body) external returns (uint8 recipe)
```

Selector `0x5add5c50` · Caller: Owner · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 141–148, 161–170

Appends an immutable recipe and returns its id, the next index. The canonical request is 1 to `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (1024) bytes, the body 1 to `MAX_BODY_BYTES` (2048) bytes, and the template must be a well-formed data template of at most `MAX_TEMPLATE_BYTES` (256) bytes; at most `MAX_RECIPES` (256) recipes exist. The contract does not check that the body canonicalizes to the request; keepers refuse a recipe whose body does not. A changed listing is registered as a new id.

**Emits:** [`RecipeRegistered`](#registry-event-reciperegistered).

**Errors:** [`OwnableUnauthorizedAccount`](#registry-error-ownableunauthorizedaccount), [`InvalidRecipe`](#registry-error-invalidrecipe), [`InvalidTemplate`](#registry-error-invalidtemplate).

#### <a id="registry-fn-registerbeacon"></a>`registerBeacon`

```solidity
function registerBeacon(address verifier, bytes32 chainHash, bytes publicKey, uint64 genesis, uint64 period, uint64 sampleRound, bytes sampleSignature) external returns (uint8 recipe)
```

Selector `0x65afb221` · Caller: Owner · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 171–187

Appends a public randomness beacon as an immutable recipe and returns its id. Its canonical request, which is also its body, is `["drand","<chainHash>"]` with the hash in lowercase hex, and its template accepts one round number: 1 to 19 decimal digits without a leading zero. An epoch it serves commits round `r` as the data, the round's scheduled time `genesis + (r - 1) × period` as the timestamp and the beacon's signature of the round, which `verifier` checks under `publicKey`. Reverts `InvalidConfig` for a verifier without code, a zero `chainHash`, `genesis`, `period` or `sampleRound`, a `sampleRound` not yet scheduled, a key the verifier does not accept, or a `sampleSignature` of `sampleRound` it rejects, so that a malformed key or a verifier that misbehaves or needs more gas cannot register. The registration, like the recipe, never changes.

**Emits:** [`RecipeRegistered`](#registry-event-reciperegistered), [`BeaconRegistered`](#registry-event-beaconregistered).

**Errors:** [`OwnableUnauthorizedAccount`](#registry-error-ownableunauthorizedaccount), [`InvalidConfig`](#registry-error-invalidconfig), [`BeaconGasTooLow`](#registry-error-beacongastoolow), [`InvalidRecipe`](#registry-error-invalidrecipe).

#### <a id="registry-fn-schedulecatalog"></a>`scheduleCatalog`

```solidity
function scheduleCatalog(uint8[] recipes, address[] signers, uint64 fromEpoch) external
```

Selector `0x42984450` · Caller: Owner · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 268–294

Schedules a catalog for epochs from `fromEpoch`, which must be at least two epochs after the current one: 1 to `MAX_SOURCES` (10) distinct registered recipe ids with one non-zero signer each, in slot order; the signer of a beacon recipe must be its `slotSigner`. Its hash is `keccak256(abi.encode(RECIPE_DOMAIN, recipes, signers))`. A pending version, one whose `fromEpoch` is two or more epochs after the current one, is replaced, so that version never applies. The version that takes effect at the next epoch is kept, as is every active one, because the next epoch's catalog is already fixed: its snapshot may be prepared and its requests open. The current epoch keeps its catalog.

**Emits:** [`CatalogScheduled`](#registry-event-catalogscheduled).

**Errors:** [`OwnableUnauthorizedAccount`](#registry-error-ownableunauthorizedaccount), [`InvalidConfig`](#registry-error-invalidconfig), [`InvalidEpoch`](#registry-error-invalidepoch).

#### <a id="registry-fn-initializereciperegistry"></a>`initializeRecipeRegistry`

```solidity
function initializeRecipeRegistry() external
```

Selector `0x8700b456` · Caller: Owner, once per proxy, as the `upgradeToAndCall` data of the recipe-registry upgrade · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 105–113

Registers built-in recipes 0 to 5 on a registry initialized before the recipe registry, whose initial catalog selects recipes 0 to 3. It runs once per proxy (reinitializer version 2) and refuses a registry that already has recipes, which includes every registry initialized by this implementation, or a catalog scheduled under the earlier hardcoded recipe ids.

**Emits:** [`RecipeRegistered`](#registry-event-reciperegistered), [`Initialized`](#registry-event-initialized).

**Errors:** [`InvalidInitialization`](#registry-error-invalidinitialization), [`OwnableUnauthorizedAccount`](#registry-error-ownableunauthorizedaccount), [`InvalidConfig`](#registry-error-invalidconfig).

Owner-only functions revert `OwnableUnauthorizedAccount` for anyone else. No setter can change a published epoch.


```solidity

```

Selector `0xd870d0c6` · Caller: Owner · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 122–135

Allows or removes a backup committer: a separate wallet that may call `commitEpoch` and `commitEpochFallback` under exactly the committer's rules, for example a follower keeper that takes over while the primary keeper is down. It has no other role, and the coordinator pays it the keeper share of the requests whose accepted proofs it submits itself. Reverts for the zero address, for allowing the current committer, for a call that does not change the address's status, and for more than `MAX_BACKUP_COMMITTERS` (4).

### <a id="registry-errors"></a>Errors

**Epoch reads**

#### <a id="registry-error-invalidepoch"></a>`InvalidEpoch`

`error InvalidEpoch()` · Selector `0xd5b25b63` · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 83, 284, 315

**Raised by:** [`epochStart`](#registry-fn-epochstart), [`getEpochSelection`](#registry-fn-getepochselection), [`getEpochFallbackSelection`](#registry-fn-getepochfallbackselection), [`fallbackOpensAt`](#registry-fn-fallbackopensat), [`checkpointEpoch`](#registry-fn-checkpointepoch), [`commitEpoch`](#registry-fn-commitepoch), [`commitEpochFallback`](#registry-fn-commitepochfallback), [`scheduleCatalog`](#registry-fn-schedulecatalog).

**What to do:** Epoch IDs start at 1; schedule at least two epochs ahead.

`error PreparationClosed()` · Selector `0x8e2a3c7d` · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 83, 330

The epoch has not started (`block.number` is below `epochStart(epochId)`), so its anchor block hash does not exist yet.

**What to do:** Wait for the epoch to start.

#### <a id="registry-error-anchorunavailable"></a>`AnchorUnavailable`

`error AnchorUnavailable()` · Selector `0x60776ed3` · Source: `EpochEntropy.sol` lines 83, 333

**Raised by:** [`getEpochSelection`](#registry-fn-getepochselection), [`getEpochFallbackSelection`](#registry-fn-getepochfallbackselection), [`checkpointEpoch`](#registry-fn-checkpointepoch), [`commitEpoch`](#registry-fn-commitepoch), [`commitEpochFallback`](#registry-fn-commitepochfallback).

The anchor (hash of block `epochStart - 1`) was never checkpointed and is outside the 256-block `BLOCKHASH` window.

**What to do:** The epoch can no longer be selected or published. Every request checkpoints its epoch's anchor, so an epoch with requests is not affected.

**Publication**

## <a id="verifier"></a>D20BeaconVerifier

The verifier of the registry's drand beacon recipe: stateless and deployed directly, not behind a proxy. `EpochEntropy` records its address in a recipe's registration (`beaconOf`) and calls `isValidPublicKey` and `verifyRound` under a fixed gas allowance. It checks the bls-bn254-unchained-on-g1 scheme of drand's evmnet: the group public key is a BN254 G2 point, round `r`'s signature is a G1 point on the RFC 9380 hash-to-curve of `keccak256` of `r` as 8 big-endian bytes, and keys and signatures use drand's serialization of 32-byte big-endian words (`x ‖ y` for G1, `x_im ‖ x_re ‖ y_im ‖ y_re` for G2). It is built on the unmodified kevincharm/bls-bn254 library recorded in `notices/PROVENANCE.md`.

Anyone can call it, for example to check a drand round inside another contract. `beaconVerifierAbi` from `@d20dao/vrf-sdk/abi` carries its ABI, and `verifyBeaconRound` in `@d20dao/vrf-sdk` computes the same check off-chain.

### <a id="verifier-verification"></a>Verification

Views, callable by anyone.

#### <a id="verifier-fn-isvalidpublickey"></a>`isValidPublicKey`

```solidity
function isValidPublicKey(bytes publicKey) external pure returns (bool)
```

Selector `0xc4c1cf54` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20BeaconVerifier.sol` lines 28–34

Whether `publicKey` is 128 bytes, `x_im ‖ x_re ‖ y_im ‖ y_re`, encoding a point on the BN254 G2 curve with every coordinate below the field order. Subgroup membership is not checked here: the pairing precompile refuses a key outside the subgroup, so a verified signature under the key establishes it. `EpochEntropy` calls it when a beacon is registered.

#### <a id="verifier-fn-roundmessage"></a>`roundMessage`

```solidity
function roundMessage(uint64 round) external view returns (uint256[2])
```

Selector `0xfd5a7458` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20BeaconVerifier.sol` lines 36–39

The G1 point that the signature of `round` signs: the RFC 9380 hash-to-curve of `keccak256` of the round as 8 big-endian bytes under `DST` (`expand_message_xmd` with `keccak256`, the Shallue-van de Woestijne map and the sum of two mapped field elements). `beaconRoundMessage` in `@d20dao/vrf-sdk` computes the same point off-chain.

**Errors:** [`BNAddFailed`](#verifier-error-bnaddfailed), [`ModExpFailed`](#verifier-error-modexpfailed).

#### <a id="verifier-fn-verifyround"></a>`verifyRound`

```solidity
function verifyRound(bytes publicKey, uint64 round, bytes signature) external view returns (bool)
```

Selector `0x3a1bc7c9` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `D20BeaconVerifier.sol` lines 41–60

Whether `signature` (64 bytes, `x ‖ y`) is the beacon's signature of `round` under `publicKey`: the pairing of `signature` with the G2 generator equals the pairing of `roundMessage(round)` with `publicKey`. It returns false, without reverting, for a signature that is not 64 bytes, a key that fails `isValidPublicKey` and a signature whose coordinates are not below the field order or not on the curve. Otherwise it runs the pairing precompile with a fixed allowance of `PAIRING_GAS`, and a direct call needs about 285,000 gas. It reverts `InsufficientGas`, and never answers false, when too little gas is left to give the precompile that allowance, so a valid signature is not read as invalid for want of gas.

**Errors:** [`InsufficientGas`](#verifier-error-insufficientgas), [`BNAddFailed`](#verifier-error-bnaddfailed), [`ModExpFailed`](#verifier-error-modexpfailed).

| Constant | Returns | Value | Selector | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| <a id="verifier-fn-pairing_gas"></a>`PAIRING_GAS` | `uint256` | `200_000` | `0x1848e02a` | Gas given to the pairing precompile (address 8). A two-pair check costs 113,000 under EIP-1108. |

## <a id="round"></a>D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood

The consumer entry point on Robinhood Chain (README [Robinhood Chain](README.md#robinhood-chain)). It implements `ID20VRF` exactly like `D20VRFCoordinator`, so a consumer compiled against `contracts/interfaces/ID20VRF.sol` and `D20VRFConsumer` works on both; the differences are in how a request is bound and read. A request binds, when it is made, the first drand evmnet round scheduled at least `ROUND_LEAD` (3) seconds after its block's timestamp, instead of an epoch packet; the result is the operator's VRF output over the request's fixed fields and that round's randomness, and the first fulfilment that serves a request of a round verifies the round's BLS signature on chain. Requests are read with `getRoundRequest`, not `getRequest`. Fees and credits are wei of ETH. `roundCoordinatorAbi` from `@d20dao/vrf-sdk/abi` carries everything below.

Block numbers (`requestBlock`) are Robinhood Chain's own L2 block numbers, read from the `ArbSys` precompile, not Solidity's `block.number`, which on an Arbitrum chain is the parent chain's. VRF proofs are checked by the stateless `D20VRFProofVerifier` and mapped results computed by the linked `LinkedRandomnessMapping` library, both at addresses fixed in the implementation's code. Requests, fulfilment, retries, `refundRequest` and withdrawals are `nonReentrant`, with the same consequence for callbacks as on Arc.

### <a id="round-types"></a>Types

#### <a id="round-type-d20vrfcoordinatorrobinhood-roundrequest"></a>`D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.RoundRequest`

Returned by `getRoundRequest`: every seed input, the result, the escrowed fee and the status of a request in one read. It does not contain the refund ratio; read `requestRefundBps`.

Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 72–92

| --- | --- | --- |

| `callbackGasLimit` | `uint32` | Gas forwarded to `rawFulfillRandomness` at fulfillment, and the lowest `gasLimit` that `retryCallback` accepts. |
| `requestBlock` | `uint64` | Robinhood Chain block of the request transaction (`ArbSys.arbBlockNumber`). |
| `deadline` | `uint64` | Request block timestamp plus `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` (60 seconds), in Unix seconds. A proof accepted in a block with timestamp at or before `deadline` serves the request; `refundRequest` needs a block timestamp after it. |
| `refundAddress` | `address` | Fixed recipient of the expiry refund and of any overpayment credit. |
| `clientSeed` | `bytes32` | Value supplied by the consumer, bound into the seed and emitted in `RandomnessRequested`. |
| `mappingHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256(abi.encode(operation, lower, upper, count, population))` of the stored spec; `hashMapping(spec)` in TypeScript. |

| `roundRandomness` | `bytes32` | The round's randomness, `sha256` of its verified signature (drand's own randomness value). Zero until a fulfilment verified the round on chain. |

| `proofHash` | `bytes32` | `keccak256(abi.encode(proof))` of the accepted proof. Zero until `fulfilled`. |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `lower` | `uint256` | NumberRange minimum; zero for every other operation. |
| `upper` | `uint256` | DiceRoll sides or NumberRange maximum; zero otherwise. |
| `count` | `uint32` | Values returned: the dice count; 1 for CoinFlip, NumberRange and ChooseOne; the number of choices for ChooseMany; the population for Shuffle; 0 for Raw. |
| `population` | `uint32` | Number of items (1 to 256) for ChooseOne, ChooseMany and Shuffle; zero otherwise. |

#### <a id="round-type-vrf-proof"></a>`VRF.Proof`

Chainlink secp256k1 VRF proof, verified by the unmodified vendored `VRF.sol`. ABI-encoded it is 416 bytes: the `FulfillmentEvidence` packet.

Source: `vendor/VRF.sol` lines 570–580

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pk` | `uint256[2]` | VRF public key; must equal `(publicKeyX, publicKeyY)`. |
| `gamma` | `uint256[2]` | Proof point. The accepted word is `keccak256(abi.encode(3, gamma))`. |
| `c` | `uint256` | Proof challenge scalar. |
| `s` | `uint256` | Proof response scalar. |
| `seed` | `uint256` | Must equal `requestSeed(requestId)`. |
| `uWitness` | `address` | Address of `c·pk + s·G`, checked by the verifier. |
| `cGammaWitness` | `uint256[2]` | Precomputed `c·gamma`, checked by the verifier. |
| `sHashWitness` | `uint256[2]` | Precomputed `s·hashToCurve(pk, seed)`, checked by the verifier. |
| `zInv` | `uint256` | Inverse of the projective z coordinate of `cGammaWitness + sHashWitness`. |

### <a id="round-requesting"></a>Requesting

Requests must come from a contract and pay at least the fee computed in their own transaction, in ETH; see README [Paying for a request](README.md#paying-for-a-request). The same functions, selectors and errors as on Arc, except that a request cannot fail for an unstarted epoch.

#### <a id="round-fn-quotefee"></a>`quoteFee`

```solidity
function quoteFee(uint32 callbackGasLimit) external view returns (uint256)
```

Selector `0xc9caa0c3` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 292–297

Fee for a request with this `callbackGasLimit` priced at `block.basefee`, that is `quoteFeeAt(callbackGasLimit, block.basefee)`. Exact inside the requesting transaction, which is how `D20VRFRequests` helpers pay. Through `eth_call` the base fee can be reported as 0, so off-chain quote with `quoteFeeAt` and the latest header base fee plus a buffer, as `quoteRequestFee` does. It does not check the gas limit range.

**Errors:** [`FeeOverflow`](#round-error-feeoverflow).

#### <a id="round-fn-quotefeeat"></a>`quoteFeeAt`

```solidity
function quoteFeeAt(uint32 callbackGasLimit, uint256 baseFee) external view returns (uint256)
```

Selector `0x26fa8481` · Caller: Anyone (view) · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 284–291

`max(minFee, feeMultiplier × baseFee × (fulfillGasOverhead + callbackGasLimit))` over the live pricing for a base fee in wei that you supply; with `feeMultiplier` 0 it returns `minFee`. A quote, not a reservation: pricing can change before your transaction. A `baseFee` large enough to overflow uint256 reverts with `Panic(0x11)` instead of `FeeOverflow`.

**Errors:** [`FeeOverflow`](#round-error-feeoverflow).

#### <a id="round-fn-requestrandomness"></a>`requestRandomness`

```solidity
function requestRandomness(bytes32 clientSeed, uint32 callbackGasLimit, address _refundAddress) external payable returns (uint256 requestId)
```

Selector `0x9849d1e5` · Caller: Any contract · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 300–305, 313–347

Creates a raw request (spec all zero) with `msg.sender` as consumer and returns its ID. Needs `msg.value` at least the fee computed in this transaction; escrows exactly that fee and credits any excess to `_refundAddress` as refund credit. Fixes the request block, client seed, refund address, fee, refund ratio (`refundBps`), a deadline of `block.timestamp + RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` and the beacon and drand round the request binds. After acceptance the consumer receives `rawFulfillRandomness(requestId, randomness)` with exactly `callbackGasLimit` gas. Checks run in this order: caller has code, refund address non-zero, gas limit in range, fee, mapping.

**Emits:** [`FeeOverpaymentCredited`](#round-event-feeoverpaymentcredited), [`RandomnessRequested`](#round-event-randomnessrequested), [`MappingRequested`](#round-event-mappingrequested), [`RoundAssigned`](#round-event-roundassigned).

**Errors:** [`ContractConsumerRequired`](#round-error-contractconsumerrequired), [`InvalidRefundAddress`](#round-error-invalidrefundaddress), [`InvalidCallbackGas`](#round-error-invalidcallbackgas), [`FeeOverflow`](#round-error-feeoverflow), [`IncorrectFee`](#round-error-incorrectfee).

Same as `requestRandomness`, storing `spec` with the request (`getMapping`, `mappingHash`). The callback still carries the raw word; read the mapped values with `getMappedResult`. `D20VRFRequests` helpers call this function and pay `quoteFee` from the calling contract balance.

**Emits:** [`FeeOverpaymentCredited`](#round-event-feeoverpaymentcredited), [`RandomnessRequested`](#round-event-randomnessrequested), [`MappingRequested`](#round-event-mappingrequested), [`RoundAssigned`](#round-event-roundassigned).

**Errors:** [`ContractConsumerRequired`](#round-error-contractconsumerrequired), [`InvalidRefundAddress`](#round-error-invalidrefundaddress), [`InvalidCallbackGas`](#round-error-invalidcallbackgas), [`FeeOverflow`](#round-error-feeoverflow), [`IncorrectFee`](#round-error-incorrectfee), [`InvalidMapping`](#round-error-invalidmapping).

### <a id="round-settlement-refunds-and-credits"></a>Settlement, refunds and credits

Recovery calls need no value or role. They forward gas to the consumer and revert `InsufficientCallbackGas` rather than forward less, as on Arc (README [Gas for refund and retry calls](README.md#gas-for-refund-and-retry-calls)); the gas figures there were measured for the Arc coordinator, so on Robinhood Chain use `eth_estimateGas` and a margin. Refund credit and keeper credit are pull balances: only the holder withdraws them.

#### <a id="round-fn-refundrequest"></a>`refundRequest`

```solidity
function refundRequest(uint256 requestId) external
```

Selector `0x7411484e` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 551–575, 587–598

Refunds an unfulfilled request once a block timestamp is after its deadline. Marks it refunded, sends `feePaid × requestRefundBps / 10000` to the fixed refund address with a 30,000-gas transfer, or adds it to that address's refund credit if the transfer fails, and adds the rest of the fee to `earnedFees`. Then calls `onRefund(requestId)` on the consumer with 100,000 gas; a failed notification does not undo the refund. The caller receives nothing.

**Emits:** [`RequestRefundedTo`](#round-event-requestrefundedto), [`RefundCallbackAttempted`](#round-event-refundcallbackattempted).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#round-error-unknownrequest), [`RefundNotAvailable`](#round-error-refundnotavailable), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#round-error-insufficientcallbackgas).

#### <a id="round-fn-retrycallback"></a>`retryCallback`

```solidity

```

Selector `0xdd11c275` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 541–549, 690–707

Calls `rawFulfillRandomness` again with the same accepted word after a failed callback, forwarding `gasLimit` (30,000 to 1,000,000 and not below the request's `callbackGasLimit`). Sets `delivered` on success. Pays nobody and never changes the word.

**Emits:** [`CallbackAttempted`](#round-event-callbackattempted).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#round-error-unknownrequest), [`NotFulfilled`](#round-error-notfulfilled), [`AlreadyDelivered`](#round-error-alreadydelivered), [`InvalidCallbackGas`](#round-error-invalidcallbackgas), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#round-error-insufficientcallbackgas).


Selector `0x054f6962` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 577–585, 587–598

Repeats a failed `onRefund` notification for a refunded request with `gasLimit` (100,000 to 1,000,000). Never transfers funds again.

**Emits:** [`RefundCallbackAttempted`](#round-event-refundcallbackattempted).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#round-error-unknownrequest), [`NotRefunded`](#round-error-notrefunded), [`RefundCallbackAlreadyDelivered`](#round-error-refundcallbackalreadydelivered), [`InvalidCallbackGas`](#round-error-invalidcallbackgas), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#round-error-insufficientcallbackgas).

Credit comes from overpayment and from refund transfers that failed, and belongs to the request's refund address, so that address must make the call. If `recipient` rejects the transfer the call reverts and the credit stays.

### <a id="round-beacons-and-rounds"></a>Beacons and rounds

Views, callable by anyone. Beacons are registered once and never change; one is in force at a time, and a change is scheduled at least `MIN_SCHEDULE_LEAD` ahead. A round is verified on chain once, by the first fulfilment that serves one of its requests, and its randomness is cached for every later one. `roundScheduleFromEvents`, `roundAt` and `replayRoundRequest` in `@d20dao/vrf-sdk/round` recompute these rules off-chain.

### <a id="round-keeper-and-proof-functions"></a>Keeper and proof functions

Proof submission is permissionless: anyone holding a valid proof and the round's signature may submit them. The keeper share goes to the submitting wallet when it is an allowed backup keeper, and to `keeper()` otherwise. Consumers normally only read `getRoundRequest`. Besides the custom errors listed, proof functions can revert with `Error(string)` messages from the vendored VRF verifier, which are not in the ABI.

#### <a id="round-fn-fulfillrandomness"></a>`fulfillRandomness`

```solidity
function fulfillRandomness(uint256 requestId, VRF.Proof proof, bytes roundSignature) external
```

Selector `0x5a58c410` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 441–459, 506–532

Accepts a proof for a request that is not fulfilled, not refunded and not past its deadline; acceptance in a block with timestamp equal to `deadline` is timely. If the request's round is not verified on chain yet, it first checks that the gas left covers the callback and the round's verification, verifies `roundSignature` with the beacon's verifier, caches the round's randomness and emits `RoundVerified`; `roundSignature` may be empty once the round is cached. It then verifies the proof against the request's seed, stores the word, proof hash and transcript hash, sets `fulfilled`, adds `feePaid` minus the keeper share to `earnedFees` and calls the consumer with `callbackGasLimit` gas. It sends the keeper share (`keeperFeeBps` of `feePaid`) with 30,000 gas to the submitter when it is an allowed backup keeper and to `keeper()` otherwise, or records it as that wallet's keeper credit. A failing callback does not revert the fulfilment.

**Emits:** [`RoundVerified`](#round-event-roundverified), [`RequestServed`](#round-event-requestserved), [`ProofVerified`](#round-event-proofverified), [`RandomnessFulfilled`](#round-event-randomnessfulfilled), [`FulfillmentEvidence`](#round-event-fulfillmentevidence), [`CallbackAttempted`](#round-event-callbackattempted), [`KeeperFeePaid`](#round-event-keeperfeepaid).

**Errors:** [`UnknownRequest`](#round-error-unknownrequest), [`AlreadyFulfilled`](#round-error-alreadyfulfilled), [`RequestRefunded`](#round-error-requestrefunded), [`RequestExpired`](#round-error-requestexpired), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#round-error-insufficientcallbackgas), [`BeaconGasTooLow`](#round-error-beacongastoolow), [`BeaconVerifierFailed`](#round-error-beaconverifierfailed), [`InvalidRoundSignature`](#round-error-invalidroundsignature), [`WrongPublicKey`](#round-error-wrongpublickey), [`WrongSeed`](#round-error-wrongseed), [`EvidencePacketTooLarge`](#round-error-evidencepackettoolarge).

#### <a id="round-fn-fulfillrandomnessbatch"></a>`fulfillRandomnessBatch`

```solidity

```

Selector `0xfdec2a74` · Caller: Anyone · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 461–479, 485–504

Fulfills up to `MAX_FULFILL_BATCH` (16) requests, one proof each, with `rounds` carrying the signatures of the members' rounds that may not be verified yet (no more entries than members). Members already fulfilled, refunded or past their deadline are skipped with `FulfillmentSkipped`, and their rounds are never verified; every other member runs exactly like `fulfillRandomness`, so an unknown ID, an invalid proof, a wrong round signature or a round neither cached nor listed reverts the whole batch. Before any result is revealed it checks that the gas left covers every served member and every round still to verify, `140,000 + Σ(callbackGasLimit + callbackGasLimit / 63 + 400,000) + 411,349` per such round, and reverts `InsufficientCallbackGas` otherwise.

**Emits:** [`FulfillmentSkipped`](#round-event-fulfillmentskipped), [`RoundVerified`](#round-event-roundverified), [`RequestServed`](#round-event-requestserved), [`ProofVerified`](#round-event-proofverified), [`RandomnessFulfilled`](#round-event-randomnessfulfilled), [`FulfillmentEvidence`](#round-event-fulfillmentevidence), [`CallbackAttempted`](#round-event-callbackattempted), [`KeeperFeePaid`](#round-event-keeperfeepaid).

**Errors:** [`InvalidBatch`](#round-error-invalidbatch), [`UnknownRequest`](#round-error-unknownrequest), [`RoundUnavailable`](#round-error-roundunavailable), [`InsufficientCallbackGas`](#round-error-insufficientcallbackgas), [`BeaconGasTooLow`](#round-error-beacongastoolow), [`BeaconVerifierFailed`](#round-error-beaconverifierfailed), [`InvalidRoundSignature`](#round-error-invalidroundsignature), [`WrongPublicKey`](#round-error-wrongpublickey), [`WrongSeed`](#round-error-wrongseed), [`EvidencePacketTooLarge`](#round-error-evidencepackettoolarge).

### <a id="round-owner-administration"></a>Owner administration

Owner-only functions revert `OwnableUnauthorizedAccount` for anyone else. No setter can change an existing request, the VRF key or a beacon registration; there is no pause, and the owner's upgrade is the only emergency path.

Affects requests created afterwards; open requests keep their escrowed fee.

**Emits:** [`PricingChanged`](#round-event-pricingchanged).

### <a id="round-errors"></a>Errors

**Requesting**

#### <a id="round-error-contractconsumerrequired"></a>`ContractConsumerRequired`

`error ContractConsumerRequired()` · Selector `0x2b99db1e` · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 140, 316

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#round-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#round-fn-requestmappedrandomness).

The caller of a request function has no code: an externally owned account, or a contract still running its constructor.

**What to do:** Send the request through a deployed consumer contract (README [Integrate a consumer](README.md#integrate-a-consumer)), and not from its constructor.

#### <a id="round-error-invalidrefundaddress"></a>`InvalidRefundAddress`

`error InvalidRefundAddress()` · Selector `0xe2fe2726` · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 152, 317, 602

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#round-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#round-fn-requestmappedrandomness), [`withdrawRefundCredit`](#round-fn-withdrawrefundcredit).

A request named the zero address as refund address, or `withdrawRefundCredit` named the zero address as recipient.

**What to do:** Pass a non-zero address that can receive a plain native transfer or call `withdrawRefundCredit`.

#### <a id="round-error-invalidcallbackgas"></a>`InvalidCallbackGas`

`error InvalidCallbackGas()` · Selector `0x35883c54` · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 142, 547, 583, 686–688

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#round-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#round-fn-requestmappedrandomness), [`retryCallback`](#round-fn-retrycallback), [`retryRefundCallback`](#round-fn-retryrefundcallback).

A gas limit is out of range: a request `callbackGasLimit` outside 30,000 to 1,000,000; a `retryCallback` limit outside that range or below the request's `callbackGasLimit`; a `retryRefundCallback` limit outside 100,000 to 1,000,000.

**What to do:** Use a limit inside the range; retry with at least the original limit.

#### <a id="round-error-incorrectfee"></a>`IncorrectFee`

`error IncorrectFee(uint256 expected, uint256 actual)` · Selector `0xdcf6afcb` · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 141, 320

**Raised by:** [`requestRandomness`](#round-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#round-fn-requestmappedrandomness).

`actual` (`msg.value`) is below `expected`, the fee computed in the request transaction. No request was created.

**What to do:** Quote again with `quoteFeeAt(callbackGasLimit, latestBlock.baseFeePerGas)` plus a buffer (`quoteRequestFee`) and resend. A contract paying in the same transaction sends `quoteFee(callbackGasLimit)`. Never quote with `quoteFee` through `eth_call`.

#### <a id="round-error-feeoverflow"></a>`FeeOverflow`

`error FeeOverflow()` · Selector `0x8181adca` · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 163, 289

**Raised by:** [`quoteFee`](#round-fn-quotefee), [`quoteFeeAt`](#round-fn-quotefeeat), [`requestRandomness`](#round-fn-requestrandomness), [`requestMappedRandomness`](#round-fn-requestmappedrandomness).

The dynamic fee exceeds the uint96 escrow limit. Within the pricing bounds that needs a base fee above about 1.3e21 wei.

**What to do:** Not expected on a live chain. For `quoteFeeAt`, check that `baseFee` is in wei.

#### <a id="round-error-invalidmapping"></a>`InvalidMapping`

`error InvalidMapping()` · Selector `0x07a966e0` · Source: `libraries/RandomnessMapping.sol` lines 19, 21–39

**Raised by:** [`requestMappedRandomness`](#round-fn-requestmappedrandomness), [`mapRandomness`](#round-fn-maprandomness).

The spec breaks the rules for its operation (README [Randomness options](README.md#randomness-options)). Declared in `RandomnessMapping`.

**What to do:** Build specs with the `D20VRFRequests` helpers or TypeScript `builtins`, which enforce the same bounds.

**Reading and recovery**

#### <a id="round-error-unknownrequest"></a>`UnknownRequest`

`error UnknownRequest()` · Selector `0x6d080297` · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 143, 643–646

**Raised by:** [`getRoundRequest`](#round-fn-getroundrequest), [`getMapping`](#round-fn-getmapping), [`getMappedResult`](#round-fn-getmappedresult), [`requestFeePaid`](#round-fn-requestfeepaid), [`requestRefundBps`](#round-fn-requestrefundbps), [`refundRequest`](#round-fn-refundrequest), [`retryCallback`](#round-fn-retrycallback), [`retryRefundCallback`](#round-fn-retryrefundcallback), [`fulfillRandomness`](#round-fn-fulfillrandomness), [`fulfillRandomnessBatch`](#round-fn-fulfillrandomnessbatch), [`verifyRequestProof`](#round-fn-verifyrequestproof), [`requestSeed`](#round-fn-requestseed), [`getProofContext`](#round-fn-getproofcontext).

No request has this ID: 0, or not below `nextRequestId()`. An unknown ID also reverts a whole `fulfillRandomnessBatch`.

#### <a id="round-error-insufficientcallbackgas"></a>`InsufficientCallbackGas`

`error InsufficientCallbackGas()` · Selector `0xa2c23f0d` · Source: `robinhood/D20VRFCoordinatorRobinhood.sol` lines 149, 455, 472, 565, 590, 698–699

**Raised by:** [`refundRequest`](#round-fn-refundrequest), [`retryCallback`](#round-fn-retrycallback), [`retryRefundCallback`](#round-fn-retryrefundcallback), [`fulfillRandomness`](#round-fn-fulfillrandomness), [`fulfillRandomnessBatch`](#round-fn-fulfillrandomnessbatch).

Too little gas remained to forward the full callback budget and keep the coordinator's reserve: `gasLimit + gasLimit/63 + 140,000` before a fulfilment callback, and in a single fulfilment that verifies its round `callbackGasLimit + callbackGasLimit/63 + 140,000 + 400,000 + 411,349` before anything runs; `100,000 + 100,000/63 + 140,000` after refund settlement; `gasLimit + gasLimit/63 + 50,000` before a refund notification; and `140,000 + Σ(callbackGasLimit + callbackGasLimit / 63 + 400,000) + 411,349` per round to verify before `fulfillRandomnessBatch` reveals any result. The coordinator reverts instead of forwarding less.

**What to do:** Raise the transaction gas limit; `eth_estimateGas` finds the minimum. A keeper sizes a fulfilment or batch to the sums above.

#### <a id="round-error-roundunavailable"></a>`RoundUnavailable`
